item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Sat Nov 14, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Evening Compline — Thu Nov 19, 9:00 PM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Evening Compline via Zoom Click here to join Compline. (This link can be used for every evening Compline on Zoom.)
The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Layer the Walls: Turn of the Century — Sat Nov 21, 3:00 PM — Ware Center for the Arts
item.description:
In one Lower East Side tenement, forty layers of wallpaper were found clinging to the walls—each piece applied by a new immigrant family. Using puppetry, masks, and live action, Layer the Walls tells the incredible stories held within each layer—an Irish immigrant helping to build the Brooklyn Bridge, Italian brothers surviving the Great Blizzard of 1888, and two Russian Jewish garment workers joining the Uprising of 20,000 to fight for safety. Recommended for ages 8 and up.

item.title: Geminids Meteor Shower at Millport Conservancy — Sun Dec 13, 8:00 PM — Millport Conservancy
item.description: [vc_row][vc_column width=”1/1″][vc_column_text uncode_shortcode_id=”128240″] Geminids are the most active meteor shower of the year! Join us at Millport Conservancy on the night of Sunday, December 13th, to observe what could be the most spectacular meteor shower of the year! Far from the city lights of Lancaster, the darker skies of Millport mean we could see up to 30+ meteors, if the weather cooperates! The Geminids are the most active meteor shower of the year, and are considered one of the two best showers for viewing (along with August’s Perseids). The Geminids are unlike most other meteor showers, in that they are not likely caused by a debris field from a comet. Instead, the Geminids have been identified as being spawned from the debris field of 3200 Phaethon, which is what seems to be an asteroid. The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.

item.title: Using Grok Bot to Recover Websites While I Sleep + 2026 Year-End Review — Thu Nov 19, 7:00 PM
item.description:
WordPress Lancaster This month, **Austin Ginder** will show how he uses **Grok Bot**, a team of AI routines, to watch and repair WordPress sites overnight. Every 30 minutes, a down-site watcher checks for outages, connects over SSH and works out what broke. When the cause is bad code, it fixes it and writes up what it changed. In its first nine days it patched about a dozen live sites, mostly while Austin was asleep.
**What we'll cover:**
* How the watcher sorts an outage: fixable, not ours, or hands off * The fix order: update, roll back, patch, and deactivate only as a last resort * Real fixes from the past month, including PHP 8 fatals, a Gravity Forms class change and a disabled PHP function * The steps after every fix: back up, purge cache, confirm the site loads, and log the change * Reviewing security signals the same way: an overnight run covered 226 findings across 206 sites * The guardrails, what it still gets wrong, and why it runs on Austin's Mac for now
